## Definitions

- [statement] Punding is a related repetitive, non-goal-directed behaviour, such as repeatedly sorting, assembling or disassembling objects; it and DDS are related to, but distinguishable from, the usual gambling, shopping, eating and sexual ICDs. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11098885/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Impulse control disorders and dopamine dysregulation · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6059034/
- [statement] Rytary is an oral extended-release carbidopa-levodopa capsule; its beads dissolve and are absorbed at different rates. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/levodopa · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery · also: https://www.rytary.com/docs/pi.pdf
- [statement] Levodopa is the principal pharmacological approach for troublesome Parkinsonian tremor; it can improve both resting and action tremor, although individual response varies. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10041452/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Tremor, gait, freezing and postural instability management · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561004/

## How it works

- [statement] Amantadine is a weak uncompetitive NMDA-receptor antagonist; the Gocovri label states that its therapeutic mechanism is unknown and distinguishes anticholinergic-like adverse effects from demonstrated direct anticholinergic activity. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label warns against abrupt withdrawal because of worsening parkinsonism and neuropsychiatric symptoms; for treatment longer than 4 weeks it advises, if possible, halving the dose for the final week. - [statement] The 2003 Cochrane amantadine review found insufficient evidence for efficacy and safety for general idiopathic Parkinson symptoms from older trials; its searches extended through 2001, so that conclusion does not include the 2017 EASE LID dyskinesia trial. - [statement] The AAN recommends using the lowest effective dopamine-agonist dose and, when stopping treatment because of adverse effects, gradual dose reduction when possible with monitoring for dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome. - [statement] Dopamine dysregulation syndrome (DDS) involves compulsive use of dopamine replacement medication beyond motor requirements, with drug seeking or hoarding, social impairment and sometimes mood elevation; distress can emerge when doses are reduced. ## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label starts treatment at 137 mg at bedtime and increases after one week to 274 mg at bedtime; it explicitly states that Gocovri is not substitutable with other immediate-release or extended-release amantadine products. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] DUOPA is carbidopa-levodopa enteral suspension delivered into the jejunum through a PEG-J tube and pump. Its March 2026 label specifies a 16-hour daily infusion, up to 2000 mg levodopa, followed by nighttime oral immediate-release carbidopa-levodopa. (low confidence) — https://www.rxabbvie.com/pdf/duopa_pi.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] The October 2024 VYALEV label permits infusion during waking hours or for 24 hours, with individualized infusion rates; the maximum recommended daily foslevodopa dose is 3,525 mg, approximately equivalent to 2,500 mg levodopa. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/216962s000lbl.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] The July 2026 INBRIJA label specifies inhaling two 42 mg capsules (84 mg) per OFF episode, up to five times daily, with a 420 mg daily maximum. Capsules are inhaled using the INBRIJA inhaler and must not be swallowed. (low confidence) — https://www.inbrija.com/prescribing-information.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] The US XADAGO label uses safinamide as an adjunct to levodopa/carbidopa for OFF episodes: start at 50 mg once daily, with an increase to 100 mg once daily after two weeks according to need and tolerability; doses above 100 mg have no demonstrated added benefit. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=c4d65f28-983f-42b4-bb23-023ae0fe81b2 · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Entacapone is given as 200 mg with each levodopa/decarboxylase-inhibitor dose; its short duration adds dosing burden, and reported adverse effects include diarrhea, urine discoloration and dyskinesia. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] The US ONGENTYS label recommends opicapone 50 mg once daily at bedtime, without food for one hour before and at least one hour after; moderate hepatic impairment reduces the dose to 25 mg, and severe hepatic impairment calls for avoiding use. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=a511a531-112e-43f8-a43f-5334b0efe979&type=display · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] The US NOURIANZ label recommends istradefylline 20 mg once daily, with a possible increase to 40 mg; strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cap dosing at 20 mg, and strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. ## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] EASE LID excluded patients with MMSE scores below 24, estimated glomerular filtration rates below 50 mL/min/1.73 m2, and prior amantadine intolerance or lack of response; these exclusions limit direct generalization to such patients. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5710325/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] Gocovri renal dosing is formulation-specific: the February 2026 label recommends 68.5 mg initially and a maximum of 137 mg daily for moderate impairment, 68.5 mg daily for severe impairment, and contraindicates use in end-stage renal disease below 15 mL/min/1.73 m2. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] NICE recommendations tagged 2017 advise against vitamin E as neuroprotective treatment, restrict co-enzyme Q10 neuroprotective use to clinical trials, and advise against creatine supplements in Parkinson disease; these adjunct supplements should not be presented as established neuroprotective therapy. (low confidence) (verified as of 2017-07-19) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] The 2021 AAN guideline allows dopamine agonists as initial treatment in selected early-PD patients younger than 60 years who are at higher dyskinesia risk; it advises against their use for initial treatment in those older than 70 years or with preexisting cognitive impairment, excessive daytime sleepiness, or hallucinations. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] In the PROUD delayed-start trial, clinical and neuroimaging outcomes did not support a disease-modifying effect of pramipexole, consistent with the AAN guideline assessment of dopamine agonist trials. - [statement] In Parkinson’s disease, clinically important impulse control disorders include compulsive gambling, shopping, sexual behaviour and binge eating; these behaviours can cause serious financial and psychosocial harm. - [statement] Dopamine agonist exposure is a major ICD risk factor, but ICDs can occur with other dopaminergic therapies; absence of agonist treatment does not eliminate risk. - [statement] The French DIGPD longitudinal cohort found independent associations of greater lifetime average dopamine agonist dose and longer exposure with ICDs. This is observational evidence; individual susceptibility and studies with conflicting dose associations limit a universal dose threshold. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6059034/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Impulse control disorders and dopamine dysregulation · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11098885/
- [statement] NICE NG71 states that when dopamine agonist therapy is started, people and, as appropriate, their family members and carers should be given oral and written information about the increased risk of impulse control disorders, which may be concealed by the person affected, and that the discussion should be recorded; a clinical review states that all patients with PD should be advised about the potential risk of behavioural addictions, especially following dopamine agonist therapy. (medium confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Impulse control disorders and dopamine dysregulation · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11098885/
- [statement] NICE NG71 states that, if a person with Parkinson's disease has developed a problematic impulse control disorder, advice should be sought from a healthcare professional with specialist expertise in Parkinson's disease before modifying dopaminergic therapy, and describes first gradually reducing the dopamine agonist while monitoring both ICD response and withdrawal; a management review tabulates reducing the oral dopamine agonist while observing for resolution of ICDs, loss of motor control and dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome. (medium confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Impulse control disorders and dopamine dysregulation · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5077247/
- [statement] The CBT trial randomized 27 patients to intervention and 17 to waiting-list control. Its small size, six-month follow-up, inability to blind participants and assessors, and lack of an active control limit certainty; caregiver burden and distress did not improve significantly. - [statement] Naltrexone has not established overall efficacy for PD-related ICDs: the 2015 management review reports a negative primary global-response outcome but improved secondary QUIP-RS scores, whereas the 2024 review summarizes the trial as a failure to improve ICDs. Secondary scale improvement should not be represented as definitive treatment success. - [statement] Wearing-off is gradual loss of dose benefit before the next dose; sudden OFF can be unrelated to dose timing, delayed ON means unusually slow benefit after a dose, and dose failure means no benefit from that dose. These are distinct response patterns. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] NICE advises against deep brain stimulation when best medical therapy adequately controls symptoms, and recommends considering it when advanced disease is not adequately controlled; the MDS review also describes escalation when less invasive options provide insufficient benefit. - [statement] NICE NG71 states that people with Parkinson's disease who are admitted to hospital or care homes should have their medicines given at the appropriate times, which in some cases may mean allowing self-medication, and adjusted by, or only after discussion with, a specialist in the management of Parkinson's disease; a pharmacy-informatics review describes electronic order entry that can mistranscribe a patient's specific medication times and intervals. (medium confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, PD medication timing, interactions and hospital safety · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10682362/
- [statement] NICE advises against abrupt withdrawal or sudden failure of antiparkinsonian treatment from poor absorption because of the risk of acute akinesia or neuroleptic malignant syndrome; drug holidays should not be used. (low confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, PD medication timing, interactions and hospital safety
- [statement] A pharmacy-informatics review states that medications affecting dopaminergic states must be used cautiously in Parkinson's disease, and singles out dopamine antagonists in the antipsychotic class (including haloperidol) and the antiemetic class (including metoclopramide, promethazine and prochlorperazine) as able to worsen Parkinson motor function. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10682362/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, PD medication timing, interactions and hospital safety · also: https://www.parkinson.org/sites/default/files/documents/safe-contraindicated-medications-2026.pdf
- [statement] The methylphenidate gait trial report states that dopaminergic treatments and currently available surgical therapies are often insufficiently effective for gait disorders in PD, and NICE NG71 recommends offering Parkinson's disease-specific physiotherapy for people experiencing balance or motor function problems. - [statement] ReSPonD was a phase 2 trial in people with Parkinson disease who had fallen, could walk unaided and did not have dementia: rivastigmine improved step-time variability during normal walking and a simple dual task, but not the complex dual task, and caused more gastrointestinal adverse effects. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26795874/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Tremor, gait, freezing and postural instability management

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the 2017 EASE LID trial, the week 12 placebo-adjusted improvement in Unified Dyskinesia Rating Scale score was 7.9 points. This is evidence for the studied extended-release product and population, rather than proof that every amantadine formulation is equivalent. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5710325/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs · also: https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf
- [statement] In the 12-week randomized TOLEDO trial, apomorphine infusion reduced daily OFF time by 2·47 hours versus 0·58 hours with placebo, a between-group difference of 1·89 hours (95% CI 0·62–3·16 hours favoring apomorphine); six apomorphine-treated participants withdrew because of treatment-related adverse events. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30055903/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] In DIGPD, among 306 participants without baseline ICDs who had follow-up, estimated cumulative ICD incidence over five years was 46.1% (95% CI 37.4–55.7): 51.5% in ever dopamine-agonist users versus 12.4% in never users. These are cohort-specific cumulative incidences, not a general population prevalence or a DDS estimate. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6059034/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Impulse control disorders and dopamine dysregulation
- [statement] Previous impulsive or addictive behaviour, alcohol or smoking history, and younger age are described as risk factors for ICDs in Parkinson's disease; these are risk associations rather than diagnostic rules. (medium confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Impulse control disorders and dopamine dysregulation · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11098885/
- [statement] Conversion from immediate-release carbidopa-levodopa to CREXONT is not a 1:1 dose substitution; use formulation-specific conversion and titration rather than matching milligrams. (high confidence) — https://crexont.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/CREXONT-Full-Prescribing-Information-August-2024.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery · also: https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/levodopa
- [statement] In RISE-PD, 506 participants were randomized; IPX203 increased daily good ON time by a least-squares mean 0.53 hours versus immediate-release carbidopa-levodopa (95% CI 0.09–0.97), with mean dosing approximately three versus five times daily. Good ON meant ON without troublesome dyskinesia. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425876/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] RISE-PD compared IPX203 with immediate-release carbidopa-levodopa in patients already experiencing fluctuations. It did not establish efficacy in early PD versus placebo or prevention of later motor complications; protocol dosing was limited to no more often than every 6 hours. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425876/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] VYALEV’s pivotal-study safety data in the October 2024 label report infusion-site reactions in 62% versus 8% with placebo infusion and site infections in 28% versus 3%; adverse reactions led to VYALEV discontinuation in 22%. These are study-specific rates, not comparisons against intestinal infusion. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/216962s000lbl.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] Inhaled levodopa (INBRIJA) is an intermittent treatment for OFF episodes in patients already treated with carbidopa/levodopa, rather than a stand-alone maintenance formulation. (high confidence) — https://www.inbrija.com/prescribing-information.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery · also: https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/levodopa
- [statement] In the foslevodopa-foscarbidopa phase 3 trial, continuous subcutaneous infusion improved ON time without troublesome dyskinesia and reduced OFF time compared with oral immediate-release levodopa-carbidopa, but infusion-site events were frequent and more participants discontinued treatment because of adverse events. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36402160/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] Safinamide adjunct trials support reduced OFF time and increased ON time without troublesome dyskinesia; the MDS review describes benefits around one hour compared with placebo, although individual trials vary. (medium confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30162 · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/
- [statement] When dyskinesia and OFF coexist on immediate-release carbidopa–levodopa, smaller individual doses given more frequently (fractionation) may help reduce peak–trough fluctuations; this is an option rather than a guaranteed response. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] For fluctuations inadequately controlled by oral medication, infusion therapies can be considered; the MDS review supports selected continuous-delivery treatments as likely efficacious, rather than guaranteeing benefit for every patient. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12089898/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label indicates this extended-release amantadine product for dyskinesia during levodopa-based treatment and as adjunctive treatment for off episodes; these are product-specific indications. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

(medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5710325/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs · also: https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf
- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label warns that concomitant drugs with anticholinergic properties may potentiate anticholinergic-like adverse effects; it advises reducing the anticholinergic drug or Gocovri dose if atropine-like effects appear. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] Benztropine and trihexyphenidyl are anticholinergic options used particularly in younger patients; cognitive impairment, confusion, hallucinations, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation and urinary retention restrict their usefulness, especially with advancing age. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/anticholinergic-drugs · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8728160/
- [statement] The Parkinson Foundation describes anticholinergics as predominantly useful for tremor with little effect on other symptoms; the Cochrane review found motor benefit over placebo but conflicting results and insufficient support for a preferential effect on tremor. The latter limits claims of established symptom selectivity. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/anticholinergic-drugs · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8728160/
- [statement] For early PD, the AAN review found greater motor improvement with initial levodopa than with initial dopamine agonists, while initial agonists caused less dyskinesia during the first five years; severe or disabling dyskinesia was uncommon in that interval. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] The AAN found no strong evidence favoring ropinirole over pramipexole or extended-release over immediate-release pramipexole for early-PD motor efficacy; formulation, administration route, cost, and patient preferences should guide selection. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety, Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] Dopamine agonists require monitoring for daytime somnolence, sudden sleep onset, hallucinations, nausea, and orthostatic hypotension; these are also explicit apomorphine-label safety concerns. - [statement] A 2024 clinical review distinguishes DDS management from usual ICD management: DDS may require reducing levodopa or fast-acting apomorphine exposure, with monitoring for motor deterioration and withdrawal and sometimes inpatient multidisciplinary care. - [statement] Levodopa is converted to dopamine in the brain. Carbidopa inhibits peripheral levodopa decarboxylation, increasing levodopa availability to the brain and reducing peripheral nausea and vomiting; it does not remove central levodopa adverse effects. - [statement] Peak-dose dyskinesia occurs at the peak of the levodopa response; diphasic dyskinesia occurs as levodopa levels rise and fall. - [statement] A common initial strategy for wearing-off is to shorten the interval between levodopa doses.
